true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "例如,大眼睛和平静的身体的女人,在草地上坐着的样子描绘的《草地上休息的女人》是与高彩的衣服和带相结合,正是梦二式的女形象体现的作品。 此外,梦二式在杂志上收集的漫画画的《梦二画集春的卷》被宣传为梦二式的女人多数出版的画集,成为畅销商。后来,在城里充满了梦二式的妇女,引发了社会现象,关于当时的梦二式受欢迎,画家木村村八回忆说:“如果不见梦二式,女学生可能已经完成了不人一样的伟大全盛。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/588f5dc5c85286438783f2302a488dbe.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "梦二手指的是不只是豪华的女人,穿着红十字标志着的衣服的骨头,抱着自己哭泣的女人,1905年(明治38)年6月在平民社报《直言》上发表的这幅漫画画,被日露战争所描绘。“平民报”等捐赠的梦二描绘了对工人和穷人等社会弱者的同情心。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/8ec6a9c9f17f674d2b5aa83ddff080e1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "梦想二式设计", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "繼續的 2 在章节中,我介绍了独特的设计性光明的工作:梦二提出,通过千代纸、封印、封面、手洗、洗衣、半尾、书籍和乐谱等设计,让人们的生活变得美丽而丰富。参见国内外的艺术杂志,同时将古代西方的艺术和工艺的形象纳入,用明亮的颜色勇敢地放置植物和地质学等,随后产生未来的新鲜设计。 梦二的设计品品,在1914年(大正3)年在日本桥上开放的“港屋画草纸店”或在大阪的“柳屋”出售,获得了普及。港屋是艺术家商品化和出售自己的作品的先驱企图,恩地孝四郎和东乡青少年以及年轻艺术家和作家也聚集在一起。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/9bdf40befda56aded47d3d00bffed831.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "木版画《港屋絵草紙店》中,由外國文化帶來的「港」和當時人們對江戸的故郷悲傷的語言「絵草紙店」組合的圖像,各自表達,港屋是木製中間口兩個小店構,但夢二手可愛的設計的千代紙、半尾等成為評價,多人來訪東京名點。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/8-5.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“晚待草”是由梦二在千葉県的 ⁇ 子遇见的女人的无果恋而诞生的,1912年(明治45)年在杂志“少女”上发表的小歌,并于1913年(大正2)年出版的书“多少”中以当前的诗形式出版。随后,在1918年(大正7)年,在东京音乐学校学习维奥林的多忠亮对这首诗感动并唱歌的《晚待草》(起初是《待夜草》),在梦二设计的表紙上出版了《Senoo乐谱》,并迅速成为流行歌。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/9-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "创建雷特罗莫丹", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "想起和新的一切,永远不会停止吸引人们,尤其是从明治末期到大正时代,即快速现代化进展的明治末期,逐渐遥远的紧张的埃多时代的记忆,以及对未见的外国文化的愿景,成为人们情感的基点。在这个时代走向绘画和物写的道路的梦二,无论是旧过去和新过去,都动心,把它们无矛盾地统一在自己的表达中。 3 在章节中,我们将注意到创建新价值的梦二的形象,这就是为什么梦二到目前为止就得到了大众的受欢迎吗?", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大正中期,作为画家迎接圆熟期的梦二,随后创造了“黑船屋”等代表作品,在“秋之<unk>”中描绘的是,在柏拉图纳斯的枝子向下倾斜的班奇上,穿着薄紫色棉花<unk>的衣服,坐在蓝色<unk>伞上坐着的女人的形象。作为制作的背景,指出的是1918年(大正7)发生的美国骚乱造成的衰退吗?从京都·嵐山的保津峡画的《嵐峡的春》和福岛的猪苗代湖画的《猪苗代的秋》中,梦二的景观画家的力量可以追溯到。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/10-3.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外,在展览会上展出近40年后的《九連環》也注目:九連環是九環組合的《中国環》所謂的智慧輪,而這個智慧輪是難解的,與男女的愛情相似的中國歌曲《九連環》在江戸時代被納加西的中國人傳達到日本,以中國語的歌詞的聲音為「<unk>之<unk>之<unk>」。」 ) 成為明治中午左右流行,穿着環帶的模型服裝的遊婦,與傳教師一起跳舞「<unk>」的,這是一個明亮的名作,與外國情緒和夢二的現代感性凝縮。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/11-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "寻找生活的美丽理想之家", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第四 4 在章节中,我们将追求梦二的记者精神和新视野的路径。 1923 (大正) 12 )年 9 月亮 1 日,相模湾震震源的巨大地震袭击了坎东,坎东大地震将东京的城市变成灰尘,梦二人受欢迎也走向终结。以 ⁇ 名的自然为心,从对与生活相关的艺术的兴趣,想象“ ⁇ 名山艺术研究所”,它是由亲密的自然和手工艺的尊重态度根源,从社会生活的变化的尖锐的视角产生的。研究所的开幕式被推迟了,因为为了观察工业艺术的目的,在回国后也未能实现,但如果这个理想乡的梦想实现,这将成为时代的活动之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/12-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "康东大地震发生时,在渋谷町宇多川的家中安全的梦二,走过被烧野原的东京,扫描了它的样子,从梦二的绘图和文字,不仅受灾的城市的样子,还传达了谣言  ⁇ 语的恐惧性,以及那些试图活得很辛苦的人的样子。在展览中,我们将接近梦二的《东京灾难画信》的文章,以及与地震有关的贴纸、报纸文章、照片等附加的宝贵斯克拉普书,进入梦二的记者精神。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外,在1931年1月(昭和6)与评论家望月百合子一起在帝国剧院观看萨哈洛夫夫妻的舞踏表演的梦二,几天后访问的望月,在表演中看到的衣服相同的萨蒙玫瑰色服装上跳舞的妇女的画作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/13-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "⁇ 名山的背景是春天女神,佐保姫,画赞,光辉的 ⁇ 名湖的美丽被唱唱,富士山的背景是秋天女神,立田姫,画赞,唐代诗人杜夫的诗歌“年春行”的一部分引用和改造,这段时间讲述了贫穷人民的艰苦生活。 2 点是, 14 每年都会展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/14-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "服装和服装的现代女孩", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "從大地震復興進進的大正未期到昭和初期,享受在城市開花的民眾文化,並且在新時尚中包裝身身上的「現代女」出現。 曾經「夢二式」的女像中一世風盛的夢二,在轉移時代,穿着衣服,剪頭短,穿着西風的裝身裝身的婦女,穿著流行的網髮的衣服穿著現代的夢二。以杂志和海报为中心,梦二产生的服装和服装的现代女孩,结束展览会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "根东大地震之后的一年创立的《妇女图》是巴黎妇女杂志为模型、时尚、艺术、室内、格鲁梅等带来的妇女图杂志。 表纸和图像是豪华的杂志,装着机械刷的木版画。 后来创立的《青草》标志着《年轻妇女杂志》、从读者发表的帖子作品,为女孩小说的流行做出贡献。梦二手,我做了很多字幕和图像。 2 该杂志对现代女孩的形象形成有很大的贡献。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/15-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "會場上也會出現「四季的女」的作品,值得稱為「未知名作」的作品,由客戶主的訂單製作的本作,先前在 ⁇ 上描繪。 6 点点的画,沿着季节的移动,从右边排序的印画粘屏风。梅底下可爱的服装的妇女在羽板上兴起的“新春”,舞妓和樱桃结合的“寿春”, ⁇ 脏的棉毛的妇女在草中休息的“惜春”,坐在潮边的妇女左手的戒指照亮的“薄暮”,落叶的树木之间的妇女在滑雪的“立秋”和穿着衣服的妇女在雪山上滑雪的“白夜”。虽然她们对梦想二画的女人有着独特的担忧,但她们用风风的发型、傘、袋、戒指等物品,都给她们带来了现代化的气氛。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在会议期间,由“minäperhonen”的创始人和设计师欢迎川明先生,并举办了专门的演讲活动,主题为竹久梦二的设计;此外,11月22日和12月22日(尼尼尼亚的猫的声音)作为“黑猫日”,梦二描绘的黑猫的原始斯特克,11月15日的“万物之日”,梦二的设计作品展出。原始斯特克,每件先装送礼物(每件都限量,消失后终止)。此外,古屋 ⁇ 丸先生的漫画“尤梅齐埃霍恩”的合作项目也出现了。每件都想享受与展览会相伴,而且,感兴趣的品品也会随时在官方网站上公布,所以这里也不会错过。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "超越“艺术”的框架,抓住时代,产生流行,人们所爱的表达者,梦二。其全形象的本展,正是决定版的内容。梦二产生的美丽和时代彩色的许多工作,在会场上,能否尝试一下? <unk>艺术展纳比)", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/17.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "⁇ 木清方《建地明石町》三部作 東京國立現代美術館「秋之プレミアム收藏」於11月15日至11月15日 所蔵作品展上7年後出現 奈良美智、藤田 ⁇ 治等", "translated": true}]
excerpt_original: 東京国立近代美術館(竹橋)で始まった「竹久夢二 時代を創る表現者」。開幕前日の内覧会で取材しました。 これぞ夢二、というレトロモダンでおしゃれな会場のデザインに思わずテンションが上がります。 夢二の最高傑作として名高い《
translated_title_zh: 【開幕】“竹久夢二時代創造的表現者” 東京國立現代美術館 時代領導的夢二的全形象接近到2027年1月11日
translated_excerpt_zh: 東京國立現代美術館(竹橋)開始的「竹久夢二時代創造的表現者」在開幕前日的內展會上進行了面試,這就是夢二、在雷特羅莫丹的美麗會場的設計上,緊張將上升。 夢二的最高傑作著名。

title_original: 自画像 47KMに生まれて
summary_zh: 《自画像 47KMに生まれて》在日本的院线上映日期为 2026-11-13。日期来自映画.com 上映安排，请在出行前核对原文。

article_text:
自画像 47KMに生まれて

劇場公開日： 2026年11月13日

解説・あらすじ

中国の女性監督ジャン・モンチーが、父の故郷である湖北省の農村「47KM村」に10年以上通い、村人と自身の変化を記録し続けたドキュメンタリー「自画像 47KM」シリーズの第6作。 出稼ぎ先から出産のために村へ帰ってきた若い女性が、カメラの前でこれまでの生活を振り返る。一方、村で暮らすある老女は、7人の子どもを産みながらも貧困に苦しみ続けた半生を語る。老いと死が色濃く残る村に芽吹いた新しい命の誕生を、監督は静かに淡々と見つめていく。シリーズを重ねる間に村人たちはもはやカメラを向けられることに違和感を抱かなくなり、監督自身も村の一部になったかのように、その日常へ溶け込んでいた。 監督のジャン・モンチーは1987年中国湖北省生まれ。中央民族大学でダンスを学び、ダンサー・振付家として活動しながら2010年から毎年「47KM村」で撮影を続けている。本作は山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭2017のアジア千波万波部門で上映された。日本初上映の5本を含むシリーズ全10本をまとめて上映する「ジャン・モンチー監督 47KMシリーズ特集上映」（2026年11月7～20日＝ポレポレ東中野）にて上映。

2016年製作／102分／中国 原題または英題：Self Portrait: Birth in 47 KM 劇場公開日：2026年11月13日

オフィシャルサイト

スタッフ・キャスト

監督

ジャン・モンチー

article_text:
Camus a écrit sept fois « l’Arabe » sans jamais nommer la victime de Meursault dans L’Étranger (1942). Dans ce récit à la première personne d’un meurtre absurde dans l’Algérie coloniale, chef d’œuvre et texte le plus lu de son auteur dans le monde, cet « Arabe » n’a pas d’identité. Une omission très discutée au fil du temps, jusqu’à sa correction par Kamel Daoud dans Meursault, contre-enquête (Goncourt du premier roman en 2015). Il le nomme Moussa, lui invente une histoire et lui donne une famille : l’écrivain algérien naturalisé français en fait, tout simplement, un personnage.

L’Arabe de Malek Bensmaïl (au cinéma cette semaine) adapte Daoud et achève de donner corps à Moussa, celui du comédien et rappeur Brahim Derris. Le frère de Moussa, Haroun, y raconte leur histoire, fût-elle fortement influencée par le point de vue d’une mère endeuillée. Dans ce récit, Meursault, narrateur dans le roman de Camus, occupe une place minime.

Incidemment ou non, ce film arrive peu de temps après L’Étranger de François Ozon (2025), deuxième adaptation, plutôt très fidèle, après celle (littérale) de Luchino Visconti en 1967. Ozon assume avoir imaginé une version« contextualisée », c’est-à-dire « prenant en compte les événements qui se sont passés après 1942 » en Algérie, de sa décolonisation à son indépendance, explique-t-il à AlloCiné .

Tout en collant au récit du roman, il change la structure et ajoute, en ouverture de son film, des actualités qui vantent « la cohabitation entre Français et Algériens » (oublié le célébrissime incipit, « Aujourd’hui, maman est morte ») puis enchaîne sur Meursault en prison : « J’ai tué un Arabe », dit-il quand les Algériens emprisonnés lui demandent pourquoi il est là.

DES FIGURANTS PRÉSENTS

Camus racontait surtout la société des colons. L’image oblige Ozon : les figurants prennent nécessairement plus de place dans le cadre, là où ils n’existent que dans les interstices du livre, qui se concentre plutôt sur ses personnages blancs. Chez Camus (que Daoud ne nomme jamais), les Arabes sont « comme des fantômes », écrit le romancier au début de Meursault, contre-enquête. Les Algériens sont ici un peu plus présents que dans le Visconti.

Pour autant, le choix du noir et blanc fige le film comme une image d’Épinal, que L’Étranger , le livre, est devenu. Question de budget limité, paraît-il, de simplicité pour les raccords des décors, selon l’interview accordée par le réalisateur à Canal+ . Mais pas seulement. « Je trouvais que ça apportait une forme de distanciation qui correspondait bien au regard de Meursault sur le monde, et puis toutes les archives de l’époque sont en noir et blanc », disait Ozon sur France Inter .

FILM D’ÉPOQUES

L’Arabe , film dont l’intrigue court sur plusieurs époques, fait aussi le choix du noir et blanc, mais pour les années 1930 uniquement. Celles où l’on creuse l’histoire de Moussa, encore vivant. On y apprend ce qui a mené Moussa sur la plage, ce qui l’animait auparavant, les filles et sa moto –lui qui était mécano. Ce n’est plus l’énigmatique « frère de l’ancienne maîtresse de Raymond », comme chez Camus. L’Étranger de Ozon, lui, nomme cette dernière : Djemila (elle est jouée par Hajar Bouzaouit).

Djemila a même un ou deux échanges avec Marie ( Rebecca Marder ), la petite amie de Meursault, qui elle aussi prend un peu plus de place dans le film. Tout comme les fesses de Meursault, érotisées dans pas mal de plans peu camusiens. Là s’arrête l’entreprise d’Ozon, qui épaissit les personnages du livre par modernisme.

▌ À LIRE AUSSI

François Ozon : « Fatalement, le cri de Meursault résonne encore »

L’Arabe joue une partition plus subtile, accordant à chacun – hormis Meursault – une place précise : chaque membre de la famille de Français qui emploie Haroun et sa mère a un nom et un trait de caractère, idem pour le personnage de Raphaël Thierry, Joseph, dont on découvre la trajectoire de vie bien dessinée, de la France à son installation en Algérie. Il aurait pu n’être que « le Français », parfait miroir de « l’Arabe », mais le film de Malek Bensmaïl va plus loin. François Ozon, lui, s’appuie surtout sur son image finale, un nom sur la tombe de l’« Arabe », pour montrer qu’il a nommé Moussa.

article_text:
“The Lowdown” Season 2 begins by giving Lee Raybon ( Ethan Hawke ) the very thing his acclaimed FX series was unjustly denied in real life: an award . For his earth-shaking exposé on Dale Washberg (aka the mystery he cracked in Season 1 ), Lee is named Tulsa’s Citizen Journalist of the Year, complete with a shiny trophy, a fancy dinner, and free booze. As much as writers, in particular, cherish that last perk, what the honor represents should matter even more. Finally, the oft-beaten but never broken gonzo journalist has proof — irrefutable, tangible validation — that his “obsession with the truth” is valued by his city, as is he, their dogged, self-identified “truthstorian.”

So, naturally, Lee belittles the gesture, along with the “liars and sellouts” who gave it to him.

High on mushrooms and his own unmoored ego, Lee’s not-quite-acceptance speech casts our protagonist as far from the heroic spotlight as anyone literally standing in one can get. His daughter, Francis (Ryan Kiera Armstrong), is embarrassed, his friends are deflated, and his audience — both the other honorees trying to enjoy their ceremony and those of us watching it all unfold through our screens — is disappointed. What happened to the committed father, community pillar, and righteous crusader who saved the day in Season 1?

That’s him. He’s right there. This Lee Raybon is the same as that Lee Raybon — only now, creator, writer, and director Sterlin Harjo catches him in a harsher light. Lee’s old self is still there, it’s whether that’s his one, true self that comes into question. Is he a force for objective good, as he believes himself to be? Or is Lee something darker and more dangerous, driven by anger and fear, while coasting on charisma and good intentions?

“There are a lot of truths out there,” a wise man says midway through “ The Lowdown ‘s” second chapter. “And the kind of truth you’re interested in, Lee, gets people hurt.”

Through six of eight episodes, Harjo’s Southern noir remains an immensely enjoyable TV series. His nimble little gem doesn’t let its core existential quandaries weigh things down, preferring to pop Lee in the face whenever he’s getting too full of himself, or tip its high-minded thoughts into delightful absurdity whenever the opportunity rises. Beautifully staged and shot in Oklahoma, the hourlong genre-bender — dubbed a comedy for its awards runs, yet equal parts honest human drama and shady sweeping mystery — is easy to sink into, surprisingly moving, and consistently funny in Season 2, even as it embraces a less-flattering vision of Hawke’s de facto detective.

Lee’s perpetual cuts and bruises can make it easy to forget he doesn’t bear the brunt of his search for truth — not the worst of it anyway. In Season 1, Lee successfully honored Dale’s wishes to restore the Washberg’s land to its rightful owners, the Osage Nation. But his quest also resulted in a number of deaths, including Arthur Williams (Graham Greene), an innocent man who was shot and killed in his own home as a direct result of Lee’s lack of restraint. Arthur’s grandson, Chutto (Mato Wayuhi), certainly wouldn’t vote to honor Lee with anything, and Season 2 often feels like it’s framed from a similar stance: through the ghosts of a past Lee prefers to forget.

One such stubborn revenant is Lee Raybon Sr. ( Tommy Lee Jones ), the father Lee previously claimed was dead. Senior, like his son, is a man of many truths. He’s a retired preacher and bookstore owner who earned the nickname “Frog” for jumping out of helicopters during Vietnam. Now, he’s an old man on his last legs suffering from dementia, just looking to reconnect with his family before his time is up.

But to Lee Jr., his dad is none of those things: He’s a grifter who conned anyone he could, including his own son. His bookstore was nothing more than an illegal porn shop, and Lee insists his father never went to Vietnam. He isn’t buying Senior’s “changed man” routine, either, even doubting his memory loss.

“Who are you?” Senior says, staring blankly into his son’s face. “Bullshit,” Lee replies.

Which is true? Which version is true? Which Lee is true — the grandfather who wants to meet and get to know his granddaughter, or the father who never cared to know his son? “The Lowdown” is simultaneously subtle and clear in suggesting, “Why not both?” Jones, a casting coup in another pitch-perfect ensemble from CDs Angelique Midthunder and Jennifer Garrett, deftly toes the line between the best and worst interpretations of his character, threading the cantankerous graybeard with grace and wisdom as well as confusion and regret. Senior is at once another inconvenient reminder of Lee’s repressed demons and his own man, back in Tulsa to “settle some scores,” whether Jr. wants to engage or not.

Where the younger Lee prefers to engage is with his new case, brought about by his new love interest. Ginger (recent Emmy winner Betty Gilpin ) sparks to the honesty in Lee’s awful speech, but she’s no rube. She sees his sea of red flags (“A good guy in a white van?” she says when he offers her a ride. “It would be history’s first!”), and carves a path between them to get what she needs: Mekko, a former client who ended up in prison, stopped returning her calls. When she goes to visit him, she’s told he’s is unavailable. When Lee goes to visit him, they bring out a different guy claiming to be Mekko.

A bad con plus his burgeoning crush are all Lee needs to believe he’s found his next big story, which means dumping his old one on Marty (Keith David), now the Heartland Press managing editor, and throwing himself headfirst into another grand conspiracy involving [deep breath] Paul Schneider as a bleached-blonde prison guard who’s weirdly proud of his sautéed cheeseburgers; Martha Plimpton as a county sheriff whose pristine manicure masks her dirty professional baggage; John Hawkes as a popular judge who wants to bring back public hangings; and returning favorites like Michael Hitchcock (as a Raybon family friend and antique dealer), Michael “Killer Mike” Render (the eye-patched owner of the Tulsa Beat), and Siena East (who runs Hoot Owl Books in Lee’s absence) along with all her cousins and buddies.

The ensemble alone makes “The Lowdown” irresistible. Such great and grand groups have been wasted in lesser series, but each talented actor gets to strut their stuff without disrupting the story or getting short-changed. With Gilpin matching Hawke’s manic energy in a combustible whirlwind of physical comedy and budding attraction, Jones provides the ideal, stoic counterbalance for his character’s spiraling son, and Harjo ropes them all together to tell a story about weighing the greater good against our immediate responsibility to others.

Early in Season 2, a friend gives Lee a tarot card reading and informs him he’s “ignoring the cup.” What really matters is right in front of his face, and he either can’t see it or he won’t. Be it his award’s true meaning, his investigation’s true victims, or his father’s true intentions, Lee runs from many potential cups, and in doing so, ends up exactly where most empowered white guys need to be: closer to the truth that exists outside his own vision. By the end of this chapter, our fearless truthstorian may have to accept there are a lot of truths out there, and sometimes, you just have to choose the ones you can live with.

Grade: A-

“The Lowdown” premieres Wednesday, October 14 at 9 p.m. ET on FX and Hulu with two episodes. New episodes will be released weekly through the finale (Episode 8) on November 25.
excerpt_original: Creator Sterlin Harjo's rich modern noir takes a closer, coarser look at our resident truthstorian in a second chapter that's darker, thornier, and still an absolute hoot.

title_original: ‘Primetime’ Review: A Sensationalisation of Sensationalism
editorial_title_zh: 《黄金时段》影评：对耸人听闻的耸人听闻化
editorial_excerpt_zh: 兰斯·奥本海姆的这部电影是全面重新审视2000年代的热潮之一。但它有什么要表达的吗？

"对于美国人对2000年代的感受，“怀旧”可能并不是一个准确的词——正如《时代》周刊2009年的一篇随笔所言，那是“来自地狱的十年”，它给我们带来了9/11事件、卡特里娜飓风、2.0版大萧条以及用之不竭的身体形象焦虑。尽管如此，人们似乎对那个时代有一种晕眩的痴迷，并热衷于对其进行重新审视。随着千禧一代步入三十岁中期和四十岁，即便谈不上文化主导地位，他们也获得了某种能带来更强购买力的职业与经济成熟度，他们对青春期和青年时期的记忆已到了丰收的季节。于是，情景喜剧如《左右做人难》迎来复兴；《穿普拉达的女王2》获得成功；萨拉·迪图姆的《有毒：女性名誉与有毒的2000年代》以及布兰妮·斯皮尔斯的自传等书籍相继问世；牛角扣大衣也卷土重来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《捉捕恶狼》（To Catch a Predator）是一档真实的罪案真人秀节目，于2004年至2007年在美国NBC电视台播出，这也是近期被重新翻出的又一个令人津津乐道的零年代现象：大卫·奥西特的纪录片《掠食者》（2025）首先揭露了该节目的内部运作并对“揭秘”这一概念本身进行了元批判；而现在则是《黄金时段》，一部未能察觉自身潜在讽刺意味的花哨剧情片。并不是说被大肆炒作的题材就绝对不能碰，但该片令人不适的重现使其不过是一部由道德谄媚雕琢而成的古装片。对耸人听闻的耸人听闻化。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由兰斯·奥本海姆执导（他还与内森·菲尔德联合执导了即将上映的《你可以看清一切》），《黄金时段》的故事背景设定在2006年，那是萨达姆·侯赛因被绞死且录像迅速流传到西方媒体的一年；也是关塔那摩湾几名囚犯的死亡进一步加剧公众对小布什政府反恐战争审视的一年。（同样在2006年：《电锯惊魂3》上映，这是该热门虐杀色情系列中票房最高的一部，它是毫无掩饰的D级娱乐与该时代对过度残酷且正义的惩罚之执念的邪恶结合。）“你难道不想让他们流血吗？”一名带有南方口音的男子在航班上对《捉捕恶狼》主持人克里斯·汉森（罗伯特·帕丁森饰）说道。这位老绅士是该节目的粉丝，他坚信汉森是在真正地为世界清除邪恶。在奥本海姆的处理下，汉森也可能是在自欺欺人，尽管帕丁森自鸣得意、眼神闪烁的表演告诉我们，这些信念不过是达到目的的手段：一个黄金时段的档期、一座艾美奖、一次晋升为新闻主播的机会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/bft_still_PRIMETIME_003_grade_dv_rec709_g24_3840x2160_20260828_87246-1230x692.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "《黄金时段》，导演：兰斯·奥本海姆，2026年，剧照。由A24提供", "credit": "ArtReview", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "考虑到汉森工作的剥削性质，这样的梦想显得十分反常，他的工作涉及诱骗网络色情狂与未成年少男少女（在节目中由成年诱饵扮演）在安全屋进行线下会面，汉森、他的摄像团队和警方已准备好在那里将他们当场抓获——即便不一定总能将其起诉，至少也能在电视上公开羞辱他们。汉森笑着对同排乘客说，后者的行为可能更糟糕，确实，该时代无论是法庭内（迈克尔·杰克逊）还是法庭外（布兰妮·斯皮尔斯）大量出现的公开奇观审判，都在提醒我们这确实可能发生。", 组织神经质的创始人泽维尔（马修·麦克费登饰）——正在他化妆室门外徘徊。随之而来的事件带有某种尴尬与矛盾色彩，巧妙地通过充满媚俗感的Y2K时代细节唤起，这些细节与被从隐蔽处挖掘出来的阴暗现实产生了令人不适的摩擦。伴随着菲姬的歌曲《伦敦桥》具有侵略性的摇摆节奏，镜头缓缓从一个带有灌木婴儿般长相的施虐者后视镜中拉远，他正在为自己与网络情人的会面自我打气。在内部，电视团队手忙脚乱，利用隐藏摄像头和传出带有金属感音频的模糊视频画面的笨重监视器监视着受害者的行踪。当汉森走下租来的麦克曼森豪宅的旋转楼梯去对质被谴责者时，他原本打算发表的英雄式独白显得漏洞百出，他那沾沾自喜的虚伪甚至比那个神经质的潜在娈童癖本身还要邪恶几分。", "电影的其余部分沉浸在这种道德的模糊不清中，这一效果是通过摄影师大卫·博伦泥泞般的影像最为令人信服地实现的。在汉森和他的团队设立据点的破旧酒店房间和空荡荡铺着地毯的起居室里，博伦的色彩基调凭借其坏疽般的色调几乎呈现出滑稽剧的效果。在其他地方，强烈的照明被刺眼地拉高，呼应了耸人听闻的录像带美学。帕丁森扮演的英俊汉森看起来像是从肯·罗素的电影中走出来的，他的皮肤在卡其色西装的衬托下呈橙色，双颊浓重地泛着胭脂红。这里展现的时代是毒性的源泉——这些视觉方案无情地表达了这一观点，而不幸的是，随着电影将黑暗讽刺演变为带有良知的恐怖片，它们也变得沉闷而丑陋。通过时代剧的戏剧化来理解过去——在这种情况下是非常近的过去——需要一定程度的历史修正主义，在这里，奥本海姆的后视镜视角过于完美地契合了当代的陈词滥调，即零年代非常、非常糟糕——与当今的冲突彻底隔绝。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿琼·辛格（Ajon Singh）的剧本围绕着一起标志着《尖峰捕食者》走向终结的悲剧事件展开：针对德克萨斯州地区检察官小路易斯·威廉·康拉德（Louis William Conradt Jr.）的一次钓鱼执法行动，当“捕食者”摄制组将他曝光给当地执法部门时，他开枪自尽了。在与电视剧《迷失》竞争收视率的压力下，汉森渴望钓到一条大鱼并迎来收视飙升，而当充满阴谋论的泽维尔透露了一个可能为政府工作的潜在目标时，汉森因有望搞出一场“水门事件”级别的大新闻而双眼放光。在自我和狂热的驱动下，汉森的行为变得愈发诡异，尤其是当一家八卦杂志威胁要发表一篇关于他的婚外情报道时。这并不是说他那位神游般的妻子（安娜·法瑞丝饰，饰演了一个戏份极少且吃力不讨好的角色，似乎纯粹是为了利用这位演员在2000年代的明星效应）会感到惊讶。", "与此同时，另一条故事线围绕着一位名叫丹（斯凯勒·吉松多饰）的新晋诱饵展开，他是一位胸怀大志的职业演员，正逐渐面对自己这门利润丰厚的新差事所带来的道德妥协。丹身材娇小、匀称，脸上带着一串可爱的雀斑，他是影片用来探索该节目幕后运作机制的装置——资深诱饵德尔（菲比·布里杰斯饰）带他熟悉了业务——也是其特定工作所带来心理创伤的体现。诱饵们通常干不长久，因此安迪敦促汉森充当丹的导师，向这个年轻人的大脑灌输关于该节目美德的种种幻觉。丹则表现得矫枉过正，把这份工作当成了一名真正演员的严肃事业来对待。他观看了一段电视访谈节目《演员工作室内部》的片段，比利·鲍勃·松顿在其中解释了他为电影《弹簧刀》（1996年）中扮演残障角色所采用的方法派演技，这一情节将丹的愚蠢行为语境化为过去那种纵容风气的症状，当时以秀场之名的运作尺度要大得多。影片悲凉而讽刺的幽默感很大程度上源于角色们的信念（对艺术、对调查性新闻）与我们对该节目劣质原则及垃圾业余性质的后设认知之间的张力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这在影片略带讥讽的前半部分里表现得相当有趣，但随着“捕食者”团队一步步逼近他们那条价值千金的检察官大鱼，充满汗渍的特写镜头和诡异色彩反转所带来的超现实严肃感，将故事推入了例行公斯的道德清算阶段。奇怪的是，它对汉森也手下留情了，无论出于什么原因，他被塑造成了一个受内疚折磨的丈夫，对八卦爆料可能给婚姻未来带来的影响感到由衷的痛苦。帕丁森展现出尼古拉斯·凯奇式的疯狂，效果虽然有些滑稽怪诞，且在某种程度上契合了他破碎的肯娃娃式神经质，但最终还是将最后一幕的泪水纷飞琐碎化了。违背“捕食者”协议，渴望开枪的德克萨斯警察部队与汉森勾结，径直闯入了检察官的家中，迎来了一个剪辑精美的高潮：画面在突袭行动、汉森目瞪口呆的面容，以及诱饵丹在电话里向最终的自杀受害者——其脑浆伴随着欢快浪漫的歌曲飞溅在窗户上——清唱音乐剧《吉屋出租》中的《爱之季》（Seasons of Love）之间不断切换。作为一场同汉森那咧嘴苦笑一样虚假的好莱坞式审判日，影片的危机被其挤眉弄眼的优越视角所冲淡，甚至可以说是遭到了破坏。除了显而易见的事实——即《尖峰捕食者》是一场源于哗众取宠和惩罚性时代的糟糕错误——它还能提供什么超越常规的新启示呢？好吧，不管内心里有何保留，让回忆复苏总是件趣事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", article_text:
Lance Oppenheim’s film is part of a broader eagerness to relitigate the 2000s. But does it have anything to say?

‘Nostalgia’ probably isn’t the right word for what Americans feel about the 2000s – the ‘decade from hell’, per a 2009 Time magazine essay, that gave us 9/11, Hurricane Katrina, the Great Depression 2.0 and a lifetime supply of body dysmorphia. Still, there seems to be a woozy fascination with and eagerness to relitigate those times. And as millennials enter their mid-thirties and forties, assuming if not cultural dominance then the kind of professional and economic maturity that gives them more purchasing power, their memories of adolescence and young adulthood are ripe for harvest. Thus, revivals of sitcoms like Malcolm in the Middle ; the success of The Devil Wears Prada 2 ; books like Sarah Ditum’s Toxic: Women Fame and the Toxic 2000s and Britney Spears’s biography; the return of duffel coats.

To Catch a Predator, a true-crime reality show that aired on NBC in the US from 2004 to 2007, is another such juicy aughts-era phenomenon to have been recently revisited: first in David Osit’s Predators (2025) , a documentary exposé of the show’s inner workings and meta-critique of the very concept of an exposé; and now in Primetime, a flashy dramatisation unaware of its latent irony. Not that sensationalised subjects should remain untouched as a rule, but the film’s skeevy recreation makes it little more than a period piece chiseled by moral flattery. A sensationalisation of sensationalism.

Directed by Lance Oppenheim (who also co-directed the upcoming You Can See Everything with Nathan Fielder), Primetime takes place in 2006, the year Saddam Hussein was executed by hanging and the footage swiftly leaked to the Western media; and when the deaths of several prisoners at Guantanamo Bay further intensified public scrutiny of the George W. Bush administration’s War on Terror. (Also in 2006: Saw III, the highest-grossing instalment in the popular torture-porn franchise, an unholy union of blatantly D-grade entertainment and the era’s fixation with excessively cruel and righteous punishment.) “Don’t you just wanna bleed em’?” says a man with a Southern drawl seated next to To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen (Robert Pattinson) on a flight. This elder gent, a fan of the show, believes that Hansen is genuinely cleansing the world of evil. In Oppenheim’s hands, Hansen might also be drinking his own Kool-Aid, though Pattinson’s smarmy, shifty-eyed performance tells us that these convictions are a means to an end: a primetime slot, an Emmy, a promotion to news anchor.

Such dreams will seem perverse considering the exploitative nature of Hansen’s work, which involves tricking online sex pests into meeting underage boys and girls (played in the show by of-age decoys) in person at a safehouse where Hansen, his camera crew and police forces are ready to catch them red-handed – if not always to be prosecuted, then at least publicly shamed on TV. With a chuckle, Hansen tells his seatmate that the latter might be worse, and, indeed, the decade’s surplus of trials-by-public-spectacle, both in the courtroom (Michael Jackson) and out (Britney Spears), remind us that this can certainly be the case.

In the film’s opening sequence, we catch Hansen rehearsing his lines for the upcoming gotcha as his minions – cutthroat producer Andie (Merrit Weaver) and Xavier (Matthew Maher) the twitchy founder of an anti-pedophile vigilante group who sources the show’s potential victims – circle the outside of his dressing room door. There’s an awkwardness and ambivalence to the events that follow, ingeniously summoned by kitschy Y2K period details that rub uncomfortably against the sombre realities being teased out of hiding. To the abrasive swagger of Fergie’s ‘London Bridge’, the camera slowly zooms out from the rearview mirror of a bush-babyesque abuser hyping himself up to meet his online paramour. Inside, the TV crew scrambles, surveilling their victim’s whereabouts with hidden cameras and chunky monitors that transmit fuzzy video footage humming with tinny audio. When Hansen descends the looping staircase of the rented McMansion to confront the condemned, what he intends to be a heroic monologue comes off as transparently scripted, his smirking artifice by degrees more nefarious than the jittery, would-be pedophile himself.

The rest of the film relishes in this moral murkiness, an effect achieved most convincingly by cinematographer David Bolen’s swampy imagery. In the shitty hotel rooms and empty, carpeted living rooms where Hansen and his team set up shop, Bolen’s colour palette is practically burlesque with its gangrenous hues. Elsewhere, the lighting is blindingly blown-out in an echo of lurid videotape aesthetics. Pattinson’s handsome Hansen seems plucked from a Ken Russell movie, his skin orange against his khaki suits and cheeks lavishly flushed with rouge. The era presented here is a fount of toxicity – a point relentlessly expressed by these visual schemes, which also, unfortunately, become drearily ugly as the film evolves its dark satire into horror with a conscience. Apprehending the past – in this case the very recent past – through period dramatisation entails some degree of revisionism, and here Oppenheim’s rearview perspective adheres too neatly to the contemporary truism that the aughts were very, very bad – closed and shut off from the conflicts of today.

The script by Ajon Singh hinges on the tragic event that marked the beginning of the end for To Catch a Predator: a sting operation targeting Louis William Conradt Jr., a Texas district attorney who put a bullet through his own head when the Predator crew exposed him to local law enforcement. Competing against the TV series Lost, Hansen is desperate to catch a big fish and secure a ratings spike, and when the conspiracy-minded Xavier floats a potential target who may be working for the government, Hansen’s eyes widen with the hope of a Watergate-level bust. Fuelled by ego and delirium, Hansen’s behaviour grows stranger, especially when a tabloid magazine threatens to publish a story about his extramarital affair. That’s not to say his somnambulic wife (Anna Faris, in a tiny, thankless role that seems only to want to capitalise on the actor’s aughts-era stardom) would be surprised.

Meanwhile, a second narrative unfolds about a newly-hired decoy named Dan (Skyler Gisondo), an aspiring professional actor coming to grips with the ethical compromises of his lucrative new gig. A nubile short-king with a cutesy spatter of freckles, Dan is a device for exploring the behind-the-scenes mechanics of the show – Del (Phoebe Bridgers), a veteran decoy, shows him the ropes – and a manifestation of his particular job’s traumatic toll. Decoys don’t stick around too long, so Andie pushes Hansen to play mentor to Dan, and fill the younger man’s brain with illusions about the show’s virtues. Dan overcompensates by treating his job with the gravity of a true thespian. A clip he watches from the television talk show Inside the Actors Studio, in which Billy Bob Thornton explains his Method-acting approach to playing a mentally disabled character in Sling Blade (1996), contextualises Dan’s folly as a symptom of the past’s permissibility, where much more was fair game in the name of showbiz. The film’s sad and sardonic sense of humour largely comes from the tension between the characters’ convictions (in art, in investigative journalism) and the retroactive knowledge we have of the show’s shoddy principles and trashy amateurism.

This plays out amusingly enough in the film’s smirking first half, but as the Predator team nears their white-whale attorney, a surreal seriousness of sweaty close-ups and creepy colour inversions shuttles the story into an obligatory moral reckoning phase. It also, oddly, pulls its punches with Hansen, who, for whatever reason, is cast as a guilt-ridden husband genuinely distressed by what the tabloid revelations might portend for the future of his marriage. Pattinson channels Nicolas Cage-style lunacy to questionably goofy effect, and though it somewhat works to forge his broken-Ken-doll neuroticism, it ultimately trivialises the tearful fallout of the last act. Against Predator protocol, the trigger-happy Texas police force, in cahoots with Hansen, heads straight to the district attorney’s home, culminating in an elegantly edited climax that jumps between the raid, Hansen’s slackjawed visage, and decoy Dan singing Rent ’s ‘Seasons of Love’ on the phone to the eventual suicide victim – whose brains splatter against the window to the song’s cheery romanticism. A Hollywood-style judgement day as fake as Hansen’s rictus grin, the film’s crisis is tempered, and arguably undermined, by the film’s winkingly superior point-of-view. And what new revelations does it offer beyond the obvious: that To Catch a Predator was a terrible mistake borne of sensationalistic and punitive times? Well, no matter one’s deeper reservations, it’s always fun to bring memories back to life.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE : Here’s your first look at upcoming R-rated comedy Mini War , starring Luke Wilson, Vanessa Hudgens, and Nick Swardson .

Capture will be selling the film ahead of, and at, the American Film Market in ten days.

Reuniting creatives behind the 2006 comedy Grandma’s Boy, the film is directed by Joel David Moore ( Avatar ) from a screenplay by Swardson and Allen Covert.

Wilson plays Joe, “a laid-back stoner who unexpectedly inherits a miniature golf course from his late uncle. Hoping to sell the property while preserving his uncle’s legacy, Joe finds himself at odds with Darren (Swardson), the ambitious owner of a neighbouring go-kart track determined to bulldoze the course and expand his racing empire. What begins as a simple property dispute quickly spirals into an all-out neighbourhood war, drawing in a colourful cast of local characters, including Olivia (Hudgens), the owner of a hot-dog stand caught in the middle.”

Related Stories

Renée Zellweger, Dominic Sessa & Peter Dinklage Set For Sacha Gervasi's High Concept Comedy Drama 'Darlington' - AFM

Four 'Star Trek' Vets Reunite For Sci-Fi 'Life 2.0', OneTwoThree Media Launches AFM Sales; Brit Comedy With Stephen Fry, Jane Horrocks Also On Slate

The ensemble cast also includes Brett Gelman, Kevin Nealon, Rob Morgan, Dave Sheridan, Blake Anderson, John Farley, Nicholas Turturro and Morgan Kohan.

Watch on Deadline

The film is produced by Jarod Einsohn (Here We Go Pictures) and Joel David Moore (Balcony 9), Limor Hakim of Level 1 Entertainment, Allen Covert, Nick Swardson, and Grandma’s Boy producers Bill Todman Jr. and Edward Milstein.

Capture is handling international sales and will present the film to buyers at AFM , taking place November 10–15, 2026, in Los Angeles.

article_text:
“ Test ,” the award-winning gay bodybuilding drama from director Sam McConnell, has been acquired by Dark Star Pictures for U.S. and Canadian distribution.

Written by and starring Brock Yurich (“Goat”), the film also features Tammy Blanchard (“Into the Woods”), Matthew Morrison (“Glee”), Paloma Garcia-Lee (“West Side Story”), Evan Hall (“Orange Is the New Black”) and Mike Edward (“M3GAN 2.0”).

Related Stories

New York's AMC Kips Bay Theater Closes on Jan. 3; CEO Says 'AMC Wants to Stay' but NYU Langone 'Wants Us Gone'

The film had its world premiere at SXSW London earlier this year and has since garnered numerous accolades on the international and domestic festival circuit.

Set against the competitive world of amateur bodybuilding, “Test” follows Eddie (Yurich), a closeted young man from small-town Ohio who dreams of achieving physical perfection and pursuing a career in bodybuilding. Living with his emotionally demanding, devoutly religious mother (Blanchard) and earning money as a cam model, Eddie channels his frustrations and desires into an obsessive devotion to his body. When he begins training under a renowned coach and rekindles an old romance, his future appears promising. But as he navigates an unexpected queer awakening, the pressures of competition, religious guilt and the dangerous world of performance-enhancing drugs threaten to unravel everything he’s worked toward.

Following its world premiere at SXSW London, “Test” has enjoyed an acclaimed festival run, with screenings at Provincetown International Film Festival, Frameline, Outfest Los Angeles and Deauville American Film Festival. The film earned the Audience Award for best narrative feature at Provincetown, the Jury Award for outstanding first narrative feature at Frameline, the Emerging Narrative Feature Award at Queer Screen in Sydney and the Canal+ Jury Prize at Deauville.

“Test” will next screen at NewFest in New York City on Oct. 21.

Written by Yurich in his feature screenwriting debut, “Test” is a production of Tandem Pictures and Hardball Entertainment, produced by Julie Christeas, Daryl Freimark and Yurich, with Jim McCauley, McConnell and Derek Strum serving as executive producers.

“‘Test’ is a bold and compelling film that offers a fresh perspective on the traditional sports drama,” said Michael Repsch, president of Dark Star Pictures. “Sam McConnell has crafted a powerful story about identity, ambition and the pressures of living up to expectations, anchored by outstanding performances from Brock Yurich and Tammy Blanchard. We’re thrilled to bring this film to audiences across the country.”

McConnell said, “‘Test’ is a film about finding the strength to be your true self and recognizing your own worth — themes that resonate deeply with me and make this story especially meaningful. Sharing the film with audiences at festivals around the world has been the most rewarding experience of my career, and I’m thrilled to partner with Dark Star Pictures, whose belief in ‘Test’ and commitment to a robust theatrical release will allow even more audiences to discover the film as we intended — on the big screen.”

Dark Star is planning a 2027 theatrical release.

The deal was negotiated by Repsch and Bill Straus of Bridge Independent on behalf of the filmmakers.
